trial_court: Chief Judicial Magistrate exercising the powers of Special Judicial Magistrate for CBI, Shimla (Cr. Revision No. 186 of 2020)
case_name: Anil Sharma And Others vs Coram

parties.respondent_defendant: Coram, Central Bureau of Investigation and another (Respondents)

facts_of_case: Jitender Kumar was married to Poonam. He died after his vehicle fell into a gorge. The informant reported the matter to the police and FIR No. 150 of 2014 was registered.

legal_principles.principle: To convict a person under Section 306 IPC, there must be a clear mens rea to commit the offence.
legal_principles.held: The Court is clear that in order to convict a person under Section 306 IPC there has to be a clear mens rea to commit the offence.

legal_principles.principle: The High Court has jurisdiction to quash the investigation and may pass appropriate interim orders as thought apposite in law.
legal_principles.held: Clearly, therefore, the High Court in the present case has misdirected itself in declining to enquire prima facie on a petition for quashing whether the parameters in the exercise of that jurisdiction have been duly established and if so whether a case for the grant of interim bail has been made out.
cited_cases: State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal
Kamal Shivaji Pokarnekar v. State of Maharashtra

legal_principles.principle: The allegations in the FIR, taken as they stand, must prima facie constitute an offence or make out a case against the accused.
legal_principles.held: This legal position was recently reiterated in a decision by a two-judge Bench of this Court in Kamal Shivaji Pokarnekar v. State of Maharashtra.
cited_cases: Kamal Shivaji Pokarnekar v. State of Maharashtra
State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal

outcome.final_order: The objections/protest petition filed by the petitioners were dismissed and cancellation report filed by the CBI was accepted.

use_for_drafting: drafting a revision petition against an order of a Chief Judicial Magistrate
